P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged but nothing read back: 'you spoke with kim i think right yeah yeah he gave me uh like a head start on you anyway'. The frame was the standard two-part version, interrupted mid-delivery by the prospect asking about the live-stream notice and then resumed: 'understand where you're at, build out what it is that you want. If there's alignment, let's talk about it. If not, that's fine as well.' Agreement requested and given ('Alrighty?' / 'Okay, cool'). Open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Only nutrition was properly asked: 'Nutrition. What kind of stuff do you eat?' Height and weight arrived inside the prospect's own opening monologue and were only picked up later inside the protein calculation. Occupation was never asked and did not emerge until 00:29:33, twenty-nine minutes in, as part of the price objection — the rep sold a $6,000 programme to a Meta employee and startup founder without knowing either fact. Age, training frequency, sleep and energy were never touched. The most serious omission is health: no question was asked, and when the prospect volunteered 'so I have an autoimmune condition, so I'm really dialed into my eating', the rep did not acknowledge it, name it, or ask one follow-up — he responded 'The good thing for you, you probably don't need that much, like, how much do you weigh, 130?'

P3.evidence: The bridge question was the best single move on this call and it worked: 'you said like you've got abs right, you've been training for a while, like you look good. Why do you want more? Because for most people dude that is like, I'm sure there's a lot of people who'd kill to be in your spot. I love the fact that you want to take it to the next level but I'm curious of why.' That produced the longevity material — bulletproofing the body, still running and playing tennis at 60 and 70 — which is the deepest thing the prospect said all call. The rep then did not build on it. He never asked what moving better would actually do for him, never asked who else it impacts, and never drove through to family, marriage or identity; there is no family information anywhere in 35 minutes. No reflect-back reframe was delivered. The one deep thread that surfaced was echoed sympathetically ('you're on a similar wavelength') rather than developed into buying pressure.

P4.evidence: The prospect volunteered a long history — years of trainers with good results, a deliberate strategy of avoiding cardio to protect calories, and a plateau — and none of it was asked about or examined. Nobody asked why the trainers stopped working, or why a self-imposed strategy that was not working persisted for years. The one check that ran, ran well: 'what do you feel like is important for you to really take you to the next level?' with the three-archetypes framing, which got a precise answer, 'I think adaptability... I don't want to see a guy that's like every time you work out you just add more reps or add more weight.' Adaptability then never reappeared in the pitch as a named benefit.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame, and on this call it is the decisive omission. For an already-fit prospect the only source of urgency is the cost of staying where he is, and the rep went the other way — he validated the status quo: 'If you're kind of in a position where it's like, well, you know, I'm already in good shape, I'm kind of happy with it', which the prospect completed with 'Yeah. The value diminishes.' The prospect had handed over a two-year frame himself, the fear of being a 70-year-old who cannot move, and it was never converted into a question about what happens if nothing changes.

P6.evidence: No commitment check, and the rep actively inverted it. Immediately before quoting the price he argued against his own product: 'Before I get into it, like what I would say to you is that you don't need to do the coaching. Every person in the world has the capability to achieve whatever they want on their own.' The belief question and the all-in question were never asked. The prospect then said 'I won't be doing that' within seconds of hearing the number.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted on the coaching. The only transaction moved was two text links to the $200/month self-guided product, which carries no onboarding call, agreement or questionnaire.

objection_plays.detail: Money trigger at 00:23:16 ('I won't be doing that') and again at 00:29:33 with a specific reason — capital committed to a startup. None of the play ran. No isolation ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%?'), no 'you're in a HOW place' reframe, no permission question, and not one of the six financial-picture questions, on a prospect who works at Meta and volunteered that his constraint was allocation rather than absence of money. Worse, the rep pre-conceded the objection before quoting — 'It's not cheap' — and offered a tax write-off that was rejected flatly. Payment plans were mentioned once, after the loss, as an undeveloped aside: 'we can break it down'.

Script gap — the reduced-scope buyer. The prospect asked directly whether the coaching could be configured down: 'if I don't need 24 seven, if I don't need X, Y, Z, is it flexible in that case?' The rep held the bundle and gave a genuine reason tied to the guarantee, which is the right answer and worked earlier in the call when he reframed 24/7 access as front-loaded form correction. But the playbook does not own this, so the improvisation stopped there rather than converting the reduced-scope request into a term or a start date.

Script gap — the satisfied optimizer. This prospect is the stated ICP in its purest form and his blocker was that he is already content: 'I'm already in good shape. I'm kind of happy with it.' There is no play for manufacturing urgency in someone with nothing wrong, and the rep agreed with the premise instead of challenging it. The consequence frame is the tool for this and it does not appear anywhere in the objection plays, so nothing prompted him to reach for it.

Script gap — the self-declared trial buyer. He described his own purchase pathway explicitly: 'I would like to start with like a Trevor guide, try it out for like a month, two months, and then be like, hey, this is awesome, I'm realizing I have some spots here that I need help, I think the coaching could take me to the next level. That's how I usually start these kinds of things.' There is no scripted ladder from the self-guided product to the coaching, no diarised upgrade conversation, and no mechanism to capture him later. He was sold the entry product and released with nothing scheduled.

notes: The strongest bridge question in the batch — 'why do you want more?' — inside the weakest overall process: no health question at all, occupation unknown until minute 29, no consequence frame, no commitment check, and the rep arguing against his own offer immediately before quoting it. Three corrections: when a prospect says 'autoimmune condition', stop and ask; never say 'you don't need to do the coaching' before a number; and when a prospect describes his own upgrade path out loud, put a date on it.
